provenance_rule: Gateway approval is retrieval screening, not scientific validation. Jansen publisher text is web-inspected and not gateway-admitted. All proposed uses require independent source review and transport assumptions. No generation, individual data, fitting, or target results used.

sources.title: Type 2 diabetes is more predictable in women than men by multiple anthropometric and biochemical measures

population.country: China, Hainan; east/southeast Asian; urban and rural
population.selection: Volunteers assessed before OGTT; broad age/socioeconomic/education distribution. Sampling frame, recruitment dates and age bounds not supplied in inspected main methods. Diabetes and medication users included.

measurements.glucose: Fasting plasma glucose mmol/L; at least 10h without food/drinks except water; 75g OGTT
measurements.hba1c: Percent; measured by standard protocols in Hainan General Hospital laboratory, detailed assay not specified

statistics.locator: Results > HbA1c predicts T2D better in females than in males (Sec2 first subsection)
statistics.effect_type: descriptive mean and SD; no adjustment
statistics.uncertainty: Pairs are mean, SD; inferential CI/SE absent. Not coefficients.

statistics.effect_type: Spearman rank correlation, unadjusted within sex
statistics.uncertainty: CI/SE absent; text P<0.01 for sex comparison

statistics.locator: Results same subsection; Fig1A caption and Methods > Data analysis
statistics.effect_type: reported linear regression lead, NOT numerically admitted for slope transfer
statistics.limitations: Text says female coefficient higher but pair order is ambiguous; figure caption describes FPG outcome from HbA1c (reverse of target). Methods say log10 conversion for visualization; precise scale of supplementary coefficients cannot be inferred. Do not invert or treat as HbA1c-on-FPG slope.

sources.full_adjustment_caveat: Table1 is binary logistic T2D outcome, not HbA1c. Adjusted analyses cite age, smoking, overweight, hyperlipidemia, hyperuricemia and T2D; this is not target conditional BMI adjustment. Main text offers no acceptable BMI|FPG,age,sex slope.
sources.overlap: Explicit reuse of data published in Li et al 2020, DOI10.18632/aging.103289 (reference39), not independently counted. No CHNS source identified.
sources.prospective_constraint: Sex-specific means/SDs and rank correlations could constrain marginal and bivariate source-context checks. They do not identify all conditional slopes or a Pearson covariance matrix.
transport_limits: Mainland Chinese geography helps relevance, but selection/date/age bounds unclear.
Verified fasting protocol differs from target unverified individual fasting and serum specimen.
Unknown treatment mix effects and no full 5-variable joint distribution.
sources.disposition: Retain descriptive/rank constraints; ambiguous slopes quarantined.

sources.title: Determinants of Glycated Hemoglobin in Subjects With Impaired Glucose Tolerance: Subanalysis of the Japan Diabetes Prevention Program

population.recruitment: March1999–December2002 health checkups; screened glucose criteria followed by75g OGTT; WHO-defined IGT
population.exclusions: Previous diabetes/gestational diabetes, gastrectomy, exercise-prohibiting illness, definitive kidney/liver disease, autoimmune disease including hemolytic anemia, ethanol>=69g/day; missing cases omitted per analysis.

measurements.glucose: Fasting plasma mmol/L and2h post-load mmol/L at central SRL laboratory
measurements.hba1c: Percent at central laboratory; assay method and NGSP/JDS alignment not specified in inspected main text
measurements.transform: Table1 median(IQR); Table2 Pearson r; Table3 Beta label without explicit standardized/unstandardized definition

statistics.uncertainty: IQR describes variation; no inferential CI/SE.

statistics.effect_type: Pearson correlation with HbA1c; unadjusted within sex
statistics.uncertainty: CI/SE absent; BMI P<0.01 male and P=0.40 female; FPG P<0.01 both.

statistics.effect_type: stepwise multiple linear regression Beta as printed; scale unresolved
statistics.selection: Candidate pool FPG,2hPG,BMI,HOMA-beta,white rice,bread selected after univariate P<0.05; age not in final models; sexes modeled separately.
statistics.uncertainty: CI/SE absent. BMI P<0.01 male, P=0.03 female. Cannot convert to percentage-point/kg/m² slope because Beta scaling and SDs are not established.

sources.overlap: JDPP subanalysis, overlapping other JDPP publications; no shared cohort with other four reviewed articles identified.
sources.prospective_constraint: Source-context Pearson correlations and quantiles can constrain an IGT-specific joint law. Table3 demonstrates additional conditional information but is unsuitable for numerical unstandardized BMI calibration pending scale clarification.
transport_limits: IGT-selected Japanese30–60-year-olds exclude diabetes; does not represent complete Chinese35–74 sample including treated diabetes.
Age not adjusted and omitted diet/HOMA/2hPG jointly differ from requested model.
Fasting plasma and assay-alignment mismatch unresolved.
sources.disposition: Partial quantitative joint constraints; Beta coefficient transfer withheld.

sources.title: Effect of Aging on A1C Levels in Individuals Without Diabetes: Evidence from the Framingham Offspring Study and the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey2001–2004

population.FOS: 2473 predominantly white community participants aged>=25, exam5 January1991–September1995; excluded diabetes defined by prior antidiabetic medication or FPG>=126mg/dL. NGT subgroup FPG<100 and2hPG<140mg/dL;59 missing2h measurements excluded from NGT analyses.
population.NHANES: 2001–2004 household sample aged>=25;3272 eligible without self-reported diabetes and FPG<126mg/dL,2 lacked HbA1c:3270 analyzed. No OGTT. Complex survey weighting.
population.longitudinal: FOS subset1704 examined again1998–2001; not the cross-sectional estimand.

measurements.hba1c: Percent, NGSP/DCCT standardized HPLC; FOS and NHANES different laboratories, NHANES boronate-affinity HPLC

statistics.locator: RESULTS, paragraph beginning 'There was no difference in BMI...'
statistics.uncertainty: Main text gives P<0.001 for FOS/NHANES and P<0.0001 for FOS NGT; no CI/SE. SupplementA3a/A3b not inspected.

statistics.effect_type: unadjusted HbA1c mean±SE and97.5th percentile by age
statistics.limitation: Illustrative source age-stratum anchors;70plus is not target70–74 and cannot be equated.

sources.overlap: Two cohorts in one article; FOS cross-sectional and longitudinal subsets overlap. NHANES2001–2004 would overlap other NHANES reports covering those cycles; no such additional original seriously reviewed.
sources.prospective_constraint: The NHANES age slope has the requested companion adjustments (BMI,glucose,sex), so can constrain an age component in its own nondiabetic source context. Does not identify BMI/glucose/sex slopes; no intercept or residual model supplied.
transport_limits: US ethnic composition, disease exclusions, age range and collection years differ.
Cross-sectional age association is not longitudinal aging effect.
Known fasting plasma differs from target uncertain-fasting serum; numerical transport requires assumptions.
sources.disposition: Retain adjusted age constraints; do not infer BMI coefficient.

sources.title: Determinants of HbA1c in nondiabetic Dutch adults: genetic loci and clinical and lifestyle parameters, and their interactions in the LifeLines Cohort Study
sources.version: Publisher full HTML as retrieved2026-11-04; published journal2013, first online2012; no correction/version label visible in inspected portion
sources.local_source_status: Exact text returned by web.open, including line locators and provenance; partial rendered original throughL367, not publisher raw HTML/PDF. Complete methods and Tables1–3 included.
sources.gateway_availability: DOI search accepted metadata but no PMCID, so fetch unavailable through this gateway. Institutional repository reports embargoed document; no access-control bypass.

population.country: Three northern Netherlands provinces; Western-European descent

model_complete_case_n.basis: 2921 minus 89 missing alcohol responses; 2832 explicitly applies to Table2 alcohol model, not explicitly to Table3 ModelIII.

population.selection: Oldest unrelated family members selected forGWAS sinceApril2009 from cohort recruited sinceend2006;3367 initially,156 diabetes(self-report orFPG>=7.0),86 significant anemia,13 missingHbA1c,10 missingerythrocytes,181 missingFPG excluded;89 alcohol responses missing.

measurements.hba1c: IFCC standardized turbidimetric inhibition immunoassay CobasIntegra800; models inmmol/mol, descriptive% also reported
measurements.fpg: Fasting fresh venous plasma mmol/L; Roche hexokinase/G6PD
measurements.gender_coding: Table3 labels Gender; explicit0/1 coding/reference not found. Do not relabel coefficient asfemale0/1.

statistics.effect_type: unstandardized multiple linear regression slopes; HbA1c outcome mmol/mol
statistics.selection: Forward stepwise clinical/lifestyle predictors with age and gender forced; waist excluded because BMI correlationr=0.80; genetics added only later inModelIV, notModelIII
statistics.uncertainty: Table labels CI without level in inspected text; record reported bounds, confidence_level=null. SE not reported. Do not fabricate95%/SE.
CI level not established from inspected text; noSE
statistics.purpose: Within-source adjustment comparison, not an independent study.

statistics.use: Slope conversion only: divide all HbA1c slopes and CI endpoints by10.93. No intercept conversion needed for slopes.

statistics.uncertainty: SDs are variation, not inferential uncertainty.

derived_statistics.status: Algebraic unit conversion, not a newly estimated target slope

sources.overlap: One LifeLines subset;ModelI–IV are same people, not independent confirmations. Hoorn is a separate named Dutch cohort, not LifeLines. Individual cross-cohort overlap not externally verified.
sources.prospective_constraint: Can constrain a source-context HbA1c conditional relationship including the eight reported predictors. Removing erythrocytes,smoking,alcohol requires their joint covariances withBMI and cannot preserve the same coefficient by assumption-free marginalization.
transport_limits: Western-European,nondiabetic,anemia-excluded GWAS subset differs materially from target.
Additional adjustment and selection prevent direct use as targetBMI coefficient.
No full covariance matrix,intercept,residual distribution or all-diabetes treatment mixture.
sources.disposition: Strongest continuous conditionalBMI lead;web admission and transport review required. No desired sign selected.

sources.title: Phenotypic and lifestyle determinants of HbA1c in the general population–The Hoorn Study
sources.version: PMC7272077.1; published article with embedded peer-review history

population.diabetes_definition: Known GP diagnosis and/or glucose-lowering medication excluded; screen-detected diabetes retained.

measurements.hba1c: Percent;firstwave ion-exchangeHPLC BioRad;secondwave DCCT-standardized reverse-phasecationexchange Menarini
measurements.glucose: Overnightfast75gOGTT plasma FPG+2hPG mmol/L;glucosedehydrogenase firstwave/glucoseoxidase secondwave
measurements.transform: Continuous predictors standardized z-scores; nonlinearBMI,hip,creatinine,vitaminC categorizedquartiles. Diet variables energy-adjusted residual method. Missing0.1%/0.2% imputed MICE5datasets, pooledRubin rules.

statistics.effect_type: adjusted BMIquartile contrasts in HbA1cpercentagepoints, referenceQ1
statistics.selection: First-wave backwardselectionP<0.10 withFPG/2hPG fixed;retained predictors replicatedsecondwave except unavailablecreatinine/fiber.
statistics.uncertainty: 95%CI explicitly inTable2; noSE. Category endpoints reproduce source rounding, not invented continuous thresholds.

statistics.effect_type: adjusted slopes for other target predictors under same fullmodels
statistics.uncertainty: 95%CI asprinted. First-waveFPG point/CI asymmetry flagged, not repaired. Table22hPG SD2.9 differs fromTable1SD2.8; noconversion assumed.

author_caution.paraphrase: Authors attribute inconsistent inverse BMI quartile pattern partly to simultaneous hip,waist,FPG,post-load adjustments and unstable closely related estimates; they avoid interpreting the inconsistent trend.

sources.overlap: Authors describe two independent Hoorn cohorts; not treated as an additional sixth study. No evidence of overlap withLifeLines; no CHNS contribution identified.
sources.prospective_constraint: Retain as a conflicting conditional association under a richer body-composition/glucose model. Quartile contrasts and rank correlations may constrain source-context sensitivity checks; cannot be converted to a linear BMI slope by dividing an assumed quartile distance.
transport_limits: BMI contrasts conditioned onwaist+hip+2hPG measure a different association from target.
Nonmonotone firstwave pattern and weak secondwaveQ3/Q4 require retaining uncertainty;noforceddirection.
sources.disposition: Retain conflict and exact estimands; no direct targetcoefficient.

global_gaps: No inspected paper supplies the full HbA1c~BMI+single serumglucose+age+female regression for an unrestricted Chinese35–74 community sample.
No complete five-variable Pearson covariance matrix or all conditional distributions identified.
Target serumglucose fasting-adherence mixture and measurement error unspecified; source fasting plasma cannot identify contamination rate.
Target diabetes/treatment mixture not constrained by the reviewed studies; more rows cannot replace missing source information.
Published associations are observational; coefficient transport is not causal effect transfer.
Source precision does not encode ethnic,calendar,selection,measurement andmodel transport uncertainty.
stop_reason: Five seriously reviewed original studies reached;10combinedqueries,4gatewayarticle downloads. Useful continuous conditional lead plus conflict and joint constraints obtained. No sixth study or quota filling.

extraction_corrections.change: Reclassified 2832 as an expected inference, not explicitly reported ModelIII sample size. Coefficients unchanged.
